_doc: Line-based scan rules. types: cs vb markup config sql proj script js ci any. pat: regexes (any match flags the line). requires: file must also match this regex. not: line exclusion. sev: Blocker|High|Medium|Low|Info. conf: Confirmed|Likely|Needs verification. effort: key in estimation.json. baseline: true when the effort is already inside the project-conversion baseline (not added twice). db: impact per database target (blocker|limited|ok). refs: ids in references/sources.md. question: open question for the client when code alone cannot decide.

rules.title: Windows registry access
rules.why: Microsoft.Win32.Registry throws PlatformNotSupportedException on Linux; there is no registry.
rules.fix: Move the values to configuration (appsettings / environment variables) backed by AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

rules.title: Windows Event Log
rules.why: The Windows Event Log does not exist on Linux (System.Diagnostics.EventLog is Windows-only).
rules.fix: Log through Microsoft.Extensions.Logging to stdout and ship to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

rules.title: WMI (System.Management)
rules.why: WMI is Windows-only; System.Management throws on Linux.
rules.fix: Replace with cross-platform APIs (System.Environment, /proc, EC2 instance metadata) or remove.

rules.title: Windows performance counters
rules.why: Performance counters are Windows-only.
rules.fix: Use EventCounters / System.Diagnostics.Metrics with OpenTelemetry or CloudWatch metrics.

rules.title: System.Drawing / GDI+ imaging
rules.why: System.Drawing.Common is Windows-only since .NET 6 (TypeInitializationException / PlatformNotSupportedException on Linux).
rules.fix: Port imaging code to SkiaSharp or ImageSharp; check fonts are installed in the Linux image.

rules.title: COM interop
rules.why: COM does not exist on Linux; the component behind it must be replaced or kept on Windows.
rules.fix: Identify the COM server, find a managed cross-platform library or service, or isolate it behind an API on a Windows host.
rules.alt: Managed library / service API; Windows EC2 sidecar as last resort
rules.question: Which COM components are installed on the current servers, and who owns them?

rules.title: P/Invoke into Windows system DLLs
rules.why: Calls into Win32 system libraries cannot run on Linux.
rules.fix: Replace each call with a managed cross-platform API or remove the feature.

rules.title: P/Invoke into other native libraries
rules.why: A native library must exist as a Linux .so build for the same API.
rules.fix: Confirm a Linux build of the native library exists (and its licence); otherwise replace.
rules.alt: Vendor Linux build or managed replacement
rules.question: Do the vendors of these native libraries ship Linux builds?

rules.title: System.DirectoryServices (Active Directory via ADSI)
rules.why: System.DirectoryServices and AccountManagement are Windows-only; only System.DirectoryServices.Protocols (LDAP) is cross-platform.
rules.fix: Rewrite directory lookups with System.DirectoryServices.Protocols (LDAP) against AWS Managed Microsoft AD / on-prem AD over VPN, or move to OIDC claims.
rules.question: Will Active Directory stay on-premises (VPN / Direct Connect) or move to AWS Managed Microsoft AD?

rules.title: MSMQ (System.Messaging)
rules.why: MSMQ is Windows-only and System.Messaging is not available on modern .NET.
rules.fix: Move the queue to Amazon SQS (or Amazon MQ for broker semantics); replace producers and consumers.
rules.alt: Amazon SQS / SNS / Amazon MQ; MassTransit or NServiceBus transports
rules.question: Which systems read or write these MSMQ queues besides this code base?

rules.title: Windows Service (ServiceBase)
rules.why: Windows services do not exist on Linux.
rules.fix: Convert to a .NET Worker Service (BackgroundService) run as a systemd unit, an ECS service, or scheduled ECS task / Lambda.
rules.alt: .NET Worker Service + ECS/Fargate or systemd; EventBridge Scheduler for timed work

rules.title: ServiceController (controls Windows services)
rules.why: Starting/stopping Windows services is Windows-only.
rules.fix: Replace with orchestration-level control (ECS service APIs) or remove.

rules.title: DPAPI (ProtectedData)
rules.why: ProtectedData throws PlatformNotSupportedException on Linux, and data protected with machine DPAPI cannot be decrypted elsewhere.
rules.fix: Use ASP.NET Core Data Protection with a key ring in S3/Parameter Store protected by AWS KMS; plan re-encryption of stored data.
rules.question: Is any stored data encrypted with DPAPI (machine or user scope) that must be readable after migration?

rules.title: CNG / CSP key containers
rules.why: CNG and CSP key containers are Windows-only (PlatformNotSupportedException on Linux).
rules.fix: Use RSA.Create()/ECDsa.Create() with keys from AWS KMS, Secrets Manager or PEM files.

rules.title: Windows certificate store
rules.why: Linux has no LocalMachine\My store; certificates must be loaded from files or a secret store.
rules.fix: Load certificates from AWS Secrets Manager / ACM-exported PEM or PFX files; terminate TLS at the ALB with ACM where possible.
rules.alt: ACM at the load balancer; X509Certificate2 from Secrets Manager
rules.question: Which certificates are installed on the servers (TLS, client certs, signing) and where do their private keys live?

rules.title: Windows file ACLs
rules.why: Windows ACL APIs are Windows-only.
rules.fix: Remove or replace with POSIX permissions / IAM policies on S3/EFS.
rules.alt: IAM / S3 bucket policies / EFS access points

rules.title: Runs Windows executables or shells
rules.why: Windows executables, batch files and VBScript do not run on Linux.
rules.fix: Replace the external tool with a library or a Linux equivalent; PowerShell 7 (pwsh) scripts can run on Linux.
rules.question: Which external tools are installed on the servers for this application?

rules.title: Windows-only UI/OS libraries in server code
rules.why: These libraries are Windows-only.
rules.fix: Remove from server code or replace.

rules.title: AppDomain creation / unloading
rules.why: Creating or unloading AppDomains throws PlatformNotSupportedException on .NET.
rules.fix: Use AssemblyLoadContext for plug-in loading, or separate processes for isolation.

rules.title: .NET Remoting
rules.why: .NET Remoting is not supported on .NET 6+.
rules.fix: Replace with HTTP/gRPC APIs or StreamJsonRpc for IPC.

rules.title: Code Access Security / security transparency
rules.why: CAS and partial trust are not supported; the attributes are ignored or throw.
rules.fix: Remove CAS attributes and partial-trust configuration; rely on OS/container isolation.

rules.title: System.EnterpriseServices (COM+)
rules.why: COM+ (EnterpriseServices) is not supported on .NET 6+.
rules.fix: Re-implement the component as a normal class/service; use explicit transactions.

rules.title: Windows Workflow Foundation
rules.why: Workflow Foundation is not supported on .NET 6+.
rules.fix: Port to CoreWF, Elsa Workflows or AWS Step Functions; or retain on .NET Framework.

rules.title: BinaryFormatter and legacy formatters
rules.why: BinaryFormatter always throws from .NET 9 and is a deserialization security risk; persisted binary blobs need a migration path.
rules.fix: Switch to System.Text.Json / DataContractSerializer / MessagePack; convert any persisted data.
rules.question: Is BinaryFormatter output persisted (database, files, session, cache) and needed after migration?

rules.title: Thread.Abort / Suspend / Resume
rules.why: Thread.Abort/Suspend/Resume throw PlatformNotSupportedException on .NET.
rules.fix: Use cooperative cancellation (CancellationToken).

rules.title: Runtime compilation with CodeDom
rules.why: CodeDomProvider.CompileAssemblyFrom* throws on .NET.
rules.fix: Use Roslyn (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis) scripting/compilation.

rules.title: Reflection-only load / Assembly.CodeBase
rules.why: These APIs throw on .NET (CodeBase is obsolete and throws for single-file).
rules.fix: Use MetadataLoadContext / Assembly.Location / AppContext.BaseDirectory.

rules.title: XSLT script blocks
rules.why: XSLT script blocks are supported only on .NET Framework.
rules.fix: Move script logic into extension objects (XsltArgumentList.AddExtensionObject).

rules.title: Obsolete WebRequest / WebClient
rules.why: WebRequest/WebClient are obsolete (SYSLIB0014) on .NET and behave differently (no ServicePointManager tuning).
rules.fix: Move to IHttpClientFactory/HttpClient.

rules.title: System.Configuration (ConfigurationManager)
rules.why: web.config/app.config do not drive ASP.NET Core; values must move to appsettings/environment and secrets to AWS stores.
rules.fix: Introduce IConfiguration/IOptions; source settings from appsettings + Parameter Store and secrets from Secrets Manager.

rules.title: System.Web dependency
rules.why: System.Web does not exist on modern .NET; every file using it changes in an ASP.NET Core port.
rules.fix: Port to ASP.NET Core; use Microsoft.AspNetCore.SystemWebAdapters to keep shared libraries compiling during an incremental (strangler fig) migration.

rules.title: HttpContext.Current (ambient request context)
rules.why: There is no static HttpContext.Current in ASP.NET Core; code deep in libraries that reaches for it must be re-plumbed.
rules.fix: Inject IHttpContextAccessor or pass values explicitly; System.Web adapters can bridge during migration.

rules.title: ASP.NET Web Forms (System.Web.UI)
rules.why: Web Forms does not exist on ASP.NET Core and has no direct equivalent; the UI layer must be rewritten (Blazor / Razor Pages / MVC / SPA) or the app retained on .NET Framework.
rules.fix: Choose per app: rewrite UI (AWS Transform can port Web Forms UI to Blazor), or retain on .NET Framework on Windows and move shared libraries to .NET Standard 2.0 (hybrid).
rules.alt: Blazor / Razor Pages; retain + .NET Standard 2.0 shared libraries

rules.title: Web Forms AJAX / third-party Web Forms controls
rules.why: Server-side AJAX controls and vendor Web Forms suites have no ASP.NET Core counterpart.
rules.fix: Rebuild the interaction in the target UI stack; check vendor licences for their Blazor/Core suites.

rules.title: Global.asax application events
rules.why: Application/session events become Program.cs startup and middleware in ASP.NET Core.
rules.fix: Move logic to Program.cs, middleware and IHostApplicationLifetime.

rules.title: Custom HTTP modules / handlers
rules.why: IHttpModule/IHttpHandler do not exist in ASP.NET Core.
rules.fix: Rewrite as middleware or endpoints.
rules.alt: ASP.NET Core middleware / minimal API endpoints

rules.title: OWIN / Katana pipeline
rules.why: OWIN middleware (often authentication) must be rebuilt on the ASP.NET Core pipeline.
rules.fix: Replace Katana middleware with ASP.NET Core equivalents (authentication handlers, CORS, static files).

rules.title: MVC child actions
rules.why: Child actions were removed in ASP.NET Core MVC.
rules.fix: Convert to View Components or partial views.

rules.title: ASMX web services
rules.why: ASMX services are not supported on ASP.NET Core; callers depend on the SOAP contract.
rules.fix: Expose the same contract with CoreWCF (BasicHttpBinding) or move callers to REST.
rules.question: Which external systems call these SOAP endpoints, and can they change contract?

rules.title: ReportViewer control (SSRS/RDLC in Web Forms/WinForms)
rules.why: The ReportViewer controls are .NET Framework only.
rules.fix: Render reports via the SSRS/PBIRS REST or URL access, or move RDLC rendering to a supported library.
rules.alt: SSRS REST API; Bold Reports; Telerik Reporting; QuestPDF for code-built documents

rules.title: ASP.NET SignalR (legacy)
rules.why: ASP.NET SignalR and ASP.NET Core SignalR use incompatible protocols; server and JavaScript client both change.
rules.fix: Port hubs to ASP.NET Core SignalR and update clients; use a Redis backplane (ElastiCache) when scaled out.

rules.title: WCF service (server side)
rules.why: WCF server is not part of .NET; CoreWCF supports a subset (BasicHttp, NetTcp, WSHttp and some WS-* features).
rules.fix: Port to CoreWCF when callers need the SOAP/NetTcp contract; otherwise re-expose as REST/gRPC.
rules.alt: CoreWCF / gRPC / ASP.NET Core Web API
rules.question: Who consumes these WCF services (internal apps, partners) and which bindings/security modes do they use?

rules.title: WCF bindings / features without CoreWCF support
rules.why: These bindings/duplex patterns are not (fully) supported by CoreWCF or have no Linux transport.
rules.fix: Redesign the transport (gRPC streaming, SignalR, SQS) or retain the service on .NET Framework.

rules.title: WCF / SOAP client proxies
rules.why: WCF clients work on .NET via System.ServiceModel.* packages, but generated proxies and client config must be regenerated and the endpoint must be reachable from AWS.
rules.fix: Regenerate proxies with dotnet-svcutil; move endpoint config to appsettings; confirm network path.

rules.title: Windows Forms
rules.why: WinForms runs on .NET 10 but only on Windows; it cannot run on Linux.
rules.fix: Retain on Windows (upgrade to .NET 10 Windows Desktop, or AppStream 2.0/WorkSpaces), or rewrite as a web front end.
rules.alt: .NET 10 WinForms on Windows; web UI rewrite; Avalonia

rules.title: WPF
rules.why: WPF runs on .NET 10 but only on Windows.
rules.fix: Retain on Windows (.NET 10 WPF) or rewrite (web / Avalonia).

rules.title: Entity Framework 6 with EDMX model
rules.why: EF6 (6.4+) runs on modern .NET, but the EDMX designer workflow is not supported in SDK-style projects and EF Core has no EDMX; metadata must be embedded or the model moved to code.
rules.fix: Short term: EF 6.5 on .NET 10 with embedded EDMX metadata. Long term: EF Core 10 (scaffold from database).

rules.title: Entity Framework 6
rules.why: EF6 works on .NET 10 but is in maintenance; EF Core is the strategic ORM (and AWS Transform can port EF code).
rules.fix: Keep EF 6.5 for the first move; plan EF Core as a follow-up.

rules.title: System.Data.SqlClient
rules.why: System.Data.SqlClient is deprecated; Microsoft.Data.SqlClient is the supported provider (different TLS/Encrypt defaults).
rules.fix: Switch to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient; set Encrypt/TrustServerCertificate deliberately for RDS.

rules.title: OLE DB / Jet / ACE (Access, Excel via OLE DB)
rules.why: OLE DB is Windows-only; Jet/ACE drivers do not exist on Linux.
rules.fix: Use native ADO.NET providers (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient) or file libraries (ClosedXML/ExcelDataReader) instead of Jet/ACE.

rules.title: ODBC
rules.why: ODBC works on Linux only if a Linux ODBC driver exists for the target database.
rules.fix: Confirm a Linux driver (unixODBC) or switch to a managed provider.

rules.title: Oracle unmanaged ODP.NET
rules.why: Oracle.DataAccess (unmanaged) needs the Windows Oracle client.
rules.fix: Move to Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core.

rules.title: TransactionScope / distributed transactions
rules.why: Distributed (MSDTC) transactions are supported on .NET only on Windows; a TransactionScope spanning two connections/resources will fail on Linux.
rules.fix: Confirm each scope uses one connection; otherwise redesign (outbox pattern, sagas).

rules.title: SqlDependency / SqlCacheDependency
rules.why: Query notifications need Service Broker (not on Babelfish); SqlCacheDependency is System.Web only.
rules.fix: Replace with explicit cache invalidation or events (ElastiCache, SNS).

rules.title: Windows-integrated database authentication
rules.why: Windows authentication to SQL Server from Linux needs Kerberos (domain-joined host or keytab) and, on RDS, AWS Managed Microsoft AD or a self-managed AD trust.
rules.fix: Switch to SQL authentication with credentials in Secrets Manager (rotation), or set up Kerberos with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
rules.alt: SQL auth + Secrets Manager rotation; Kerberos via AWS Managed Microsoft AD
rules.question: Must database access keep using Windows (Kerberos) identities for audit/compliance?

rules.title: SQL CLR assemblies
rules.why: CLR is not supported on RDS for SQL Server 2017+ (SAFE only on 2016 and lower) nor on Babelfish.
rules.fix: Rewrite CLR routines in T-SQL or move logic to the application / Lambda; or use SQL Server on EC2.
rules.alt: T-SQL / app code / Lambda; SQL Server on EC2

rules.title: Linked servers / distributed queries
rules.why: RDS supports linked servers only in limited forms; Babelfish allows read-only four-part names to SQL Server targets.
rules.fix: Inventory each linked server; replace with application-level integration or AWS DMS replication where possible.
rules.question: What do the linked servers point at, and will those systems also move to AWS?

rules.title: xp_cmdshell / OLE automation / file-system extended procedures
rules.why: Extended stored procedures and OS access are not available on RDS or Babelfish.
rules.fix: Move OS/file work into the application or a Lambda/ECS task; use S3 integration for files.
rules.alt: Lambda / ECS task / RDS S3 integration

rules.title: FILESTREAM / FileTable
rules.why: FILESTREAM and FileTables are not supported on RDS or Babelfish.
rules.fix: Store blobs in Amazon S3 with keys in the database.

rules.title: Service Broker
rules.why: RDS does not support Service Broker endpoints (cross-instance); Babelfish has no Service Broker.
rules.fix: Replace with Amazon SQS/SNS or an outbox table polled by a worker.

rules.title: Distributed transactions in T-SQL
rules.why: MSDTC needs an option group on RDS and is unsupported on Babelfish.
rules.fix: Avoid cross-server transactions; redesign with sagas/outbox.

rules.title: SQL Server Agent jobs
rules.why: SQL Agent is available on RDS (msdb import not supported) but not on Babelfish.
rules.fix: Recreate jobs on RDS, or move them to EventBridge Scheduler + Lambda/ECS for Babelfish/PostgreSQL.
rules.question: Which SQL Agent jobs run on the current server (the repository may not contain all of them)?

rules.title: Cross-database references (three-part names)
rules.why: Cross-database queries work on one RDS instance (all databases must move together) and in Babelfish multi-database mode only for DML, not DDL.
rules.fix: Keep the related databases on the same instance, or remove the coupling.

rules.title: BULK INSERT / OPENROWSET(BULK) from server files
rules.why: There is no server file system on RDS (use S3 integration) and BULK INSERT is not supported on Babelfish.
rules.fix: Load files through the application, AWS DMS/Glue, or RDS S3 integration.

rules.title: Full-text search
rules.why: Full-text search works on RDS for SQL Server but is not supported by Babelfish.
rules.fix: RDS: keep. Babelfish/PostgreSQL: move to PostgreSQL full-text or Amazon OpenSearch.

rules.title: T-SQL syntax not supported by Babelfish
rules.why: Babelfish does not support these constructs (see the AWS list of unsupported functionality); RDS for SQL Server does.
rules.fix: Rewrite each construct before choosing Babelfish; confirm with Babelfish Compass on a schema export.

rules.title: Server-level configuration / privileges
rules.why: RDS gives no sysadmin: sp_configure, TRUSTWORTHY, server triggers, endpoints and replication are unsupported (parameter groups replace sp_configure).
rules.fix: Translate settings to RDS parameter groups; remove server-level objects or use SQL Server on EC2.
rules.alt: RDS parameter/option groups; SQL Server on EC2

rules.title: Database Mail
rules.why: Database Mail works on RDS (with configuration) but not on Babelfish.
rules.fix: Send email from the application through Amazon SES.

rules.title: Windows authentication / impersonation in IIS
rules.why: On Linux, Windows auth needs the Negotiate handler with Kerberos (keytab, SPNs, LDAP for roles); impersonation is Windows-only.
rules.fix: Move users to an OIDC identity provider (IAM Identity Center, Cognito, Entra ID via federation) or configure Negotiate/Kerberos with AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
rules.alt: OIDC (Cognito / Entra ID / ADFS OIDC); Negotiate + keytab
rules.question: Do users sign in with domain accounts, and is a move to SSO/OIDC acceptable?

rules.title: Windows identity / impersonation in code
rules.why: WindowsIdentity and impersonation are Windows-only.
rules.fix: Use claims from the identity provider; access resources with IAM roles instead of impersonated accounts.

rules.title: Forms authentication / Membership / Role manager
rules.why: Forms auth tickets and Membership providers do not exist in ASP.NET Core; password hashes need a migration strategy.
rules.fix: Move to ASP.NET Core cookie authentication + ASP.NET Core Identity (or an external IdP); migrate users with a rehash-on-login strategy.

rules.title: machineKey configuration
rules.why: machineKey protects auth cookies, ViewState and anti-forgery tokens; ASP.NET Core uses the Data Protection key ring, and web farms need shared keys.
rules.fix: Store keys in Secrets Manager (never in config); share a Data Protection key ring (S3 + KMS) across instances; plan cookie compatibility during cut-over.

rules.title: WS-Federation / ADFS (WIF)
rules.why: Windows Identity Foundation is .NET Framework only.
rules.fix: Use Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.WsFederation or switch the relying party to OIDC.
rules.question: Which identity provider (ADFS version, Entra ID) issues tokens, and will it be reachable from AWS?

rules.title: ASP.NET Identity 2 (OWIN)
rules.why: ASP.NET Identity 2 must move to ASP.NET Core Identity (schema and hasher differ).
rules.fix: Migrate to ASP.NET Core Identity; keep the v2 password hasher compatibility mode during transition.

rules.title: Outbound calls with Windows default credentials
rules.why: On Linux the process has no Windows identity; integrated auth to on-prem services needs Kerberos configuration.
rules.fix: Use explicit service credentials from Secrets Manager or Kerberos keytabs.

rules.title: External identity provider (OpenID Connect / Azure AD / Entra ID)
rules.why: Sign-in is delegated to an external IdP: the OWIN middleware must be replaced, and redirect URIs, client secrets and allowed origins must be registered for the new AWS host names.
rules.fix: Port to ASP.NET Core OpenID Connect (or Microsoft.Identity.Web); register AWS redirect URIs; move client secrets to Secrets Manager.
rules.question: Which identity provider tenant/app registrations does each application use, and who can add the new redirect URIs?

rules.title: Hard-coded credential or key in source
rules.why: Credentials in source code travel with every clone and cannot be rotated.
rules.fix: Move to AWS Secrets Manager; rotate the exposed credential.

rules.title: DPAPI/RSA-protected configuration sections
rules.why: Protected config sections are machine-bound and RsaProtectedConfigurationProvider throws on .NET.
rules.fix: Move the protected values to Secrets Manager / Parameter Store (SecureString).

rules.title: web.config / app.config transforms
rules.why: Per-environment transforms become appsettings.{Environment}.json + environment variables.
rules.fix: Map each transform to environment configuration and Parameter Store paths.

rules.title: UNC network share paths
rules.why: SMB shares on the on-prem network are unreachable from AWS without VPN/Direct Connect, and Linux needs a mount instead of UNC paths.
rules.fix: Move the files to Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, or FSx for Windows File Server / FSx for NetApp ONTAP (SMB); use configuration, not literals.
rules.question: What lives on these shares, how big is it, and which other systems read or write it?

rules.title: SMTP email sending
rules.why: On-prem SMTP relays are not reachable from AWS without a network path; EC2 throttles outbound port 25.
rules.fix: Send through Amazon SES (SMTP interface or API) with verified domains (SPF/DKIM/DMARC).
rules.question: Which SMTP relay is used today and are there allow-listed sender IPs?

rules.title: FTP/SFTP transfers
rules.why: File-transfer partners usually allow-list source IPs; the egress IP changes on AWS.
rules.fix: Use fixed egress IPs (NAT gateway Elastic IPs) and notify partners; consider AWS Transfer Family for inbound.
rules.alt: AWS Transfer Family; NAT gateway EIPs
rules.question: Which partners exchange files, and do they allow-list our IP addresses?

rules.title: Explicit HTTP proxy configuration
rules.why: Corporate proxies are usually not reachable or not wanted from AWS.
rules.fix: Remove or make egress configurable (VPC endpoints / NAT).

rules.title: Hardware / MAC / BIOS identifiers
rules.why: Licensing or identity tied to hardware/MAC/BIOS breaks when VMs move hypervisor or instances are replaced.
rules.fix: Find what the identifier is used for (often licensing); move to instance-independent identity or re-license.
rules.question: Is any software licensed to a MAC address, host ID or BIOS serial on the current VMs?

rules.title: Logic keyed on machine name / host name
rules.why: Host names change on AWS (auto scaling, containers); logic that switches on server name breaks.
rules.fix: Use explicit configuration/environment instead of host names.

rules.title: Local devices (serial/COM/LPT ports, dongles, scanners)
rules.why: Physical devices attached to an on-prem host cannot follow the workload to AWS.
rules.fix: Move the device interaction to an edge component (e.g. on-prem agent, IoT Greengrass) or retire it.
rules.question: Are any devices physically attached to the servers (ports, dongles, scanners, printers)?

rules.title: Hard-coded drive-letter paths
rules.why: Linux has no drive letters; these paths fail on Linux and on any new host.
rules.fix: Make paths configurable and root them in a mounted volume / S3.

rules.title: Backslash path separators in literals
rules.why: '\' is a valid file-name character on Linux, so these paths silently point to the wrong place.
rules.fix: Use Path.Combine / '/' separators.

rules.title: Server.MapPath / HostingEnvironment.MapPath
rules.why: MapPath does not exist in ASP.NET Core; files under the site folder are lost when containers restart.
rules.fix: Use IWebHostEnvironment.ContentRootPath/WebRootPath for read-only assets; S3/EFS for writable data.

rules.title: Windows special folders / %VARIABLES%
rules.why: These locations do not exist (or map to unexpected paths) on Linux/containers.
rules.fix: Use configured paths on mounted storage.

rules.title: Writes to the local file system
rules.why: Local disk is not shared between instances and is lost with containers; files written here break horizontal scaling.
rules.fix: Write durable files to Amazon S3 (or EFS when a file system is required); keep only temp files locally.

rules.title: Code-page encodings / Encoding.Default
rules.why: Encoding.Default is UTF-8 on .NET (ANSI code page on .NET Framework); code pages need CodePagesEncodingProvider.
rules.fix: Name encodings explicitly; register CodePagesEncodingProvider where legacy code pages are needed.

rules.title: Hard-coded CRLF line endings
rules.why: Environment.NewLine is \n on Linux; parsers that split on \r\n or files compared byte-for-byte behave differently.
rules.fix: Decide per use: protocol-mandated CRLF (keep), file output (Environment.NewLine or explicit), parsing (accept both).

rules.title: IIS URL Rewrite rules
rules.why: IIS URL Rewrite is an IIS module; rules must move to ASP.NET Core rewrite middleware or the load balancer.
rules.fix: Translate rules to UseRewriter (it can import IIS rules) or ALB listener rules / CloudFront functions.

rules.title: IIS modules and handlers registered in config
rules.why: Module/handler registrations configure IIS; each needs an ASP.NET Core equivalent.
rules.fix: Map each registered module/handler to middleware or remove.

rules.title: Session state mode
rules.why: In-process session needs sticky sessions and is lost on restart; StateServer/SQLServer modes are System.Web features.
rules.fix: Use ASP.NET Core distributed session backed by ElastiCache (Redis/Valkey) or DynamoDB; reduce session usage.

rules.title: httpRuntime / request limits
rules.why: Upload size and timeouts move to Kestrel/ALB settings.
rules.fix: Set KestrelServerOptions/FormOptions limits and ALB idle timeout.

rules.title: IIS / MSDeploy publishing
rules.why: Deployment targets IIS today.
rules.fix: Replace with container images (ECR) or Linux packages deployed by CodePipeline/GitHub Actions.

rules.title: Windows container images
rules.why: Windows containers keep Windows licensing and run only on Windows nodes (ECS Windows / EKS Windows).
rules.fix: After porting, rebuild on Linux images (mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0); otherwise run on ECS with Windows container instances.
rules.alt: Linux .NET 10 images; ECS Windows as fallback

rules.title: In-process application state / cache
rules.why: Each instance gets its own copy; data diverges once the app runs on more than one server.
rules.fix: Use IDistributedCache on ElastiCache for shared data; keep IMemoryCache only for per-instance, rebuildable data.

rules.title: Session usage in code
rules.why: Session values must be serializable and stored out of process to scale horizontally; ASP.NET Core session stores bytes/strings only.
rules.fix: Minimise session; store in distributed session (ElastiCache) with JSON serialization.

rules.title: Static mutable collections (per-process state)
rules.why: Static collections act as per-instance caches/state; behaviour changes when scaled out.
rules.fix: Review each: keep if rebuildable per instance, otherwise move to a shared store.

rules.title: Timers / background work inside web processes
rules.why: In-process timers run once per instance after scale-out and stop when the app pool/container recycles.
rules.fix: Move scheduled work to a hosted worker with a distributed lock, or to EventBridge Scheduler + Lambda/ECS tasks.

rules.title: Windows Task Scheduler
rules.why: Task Scheduler is Windows-only; jobs scheduled on the server are often undocumented.
rules.fix: Move schedules to EventBridge Scheduler (cron) triggering ECS tasks/Lambda.
rules.question: List every scheduled task on the current servers (the repository rarely contains all of them).

rules.title: Hangfire / Quartz.NET job schedulers
rules.why: Both run on .NET 10; scaled-out instances need clustered/shared job storage and dashboard authorization.
rules.fix: Use persistent job storage (SQL/Redis) and clustering; secure the dashboard.

rules.title: File-based logging targets
rules.why: Log files on instance disks are lost with containers and are not centralised; Event Log targets fail on Linux.
rules.fix: Log to stdout in JSON and collect with CloudWatch Logs (awslogs / FireLens) or use CloudWatch sinks.

rules.title: ELMAH error logging
rules.why: ELMAH classic is System.Web-based.
rules.fix: Use ASP.NET Core exception handling middleware + CloudWatch/X-Ray (or ElmahCore).

rules.title: System.Diagnostics trace listeners
rules.why: Config-driven trace listeners are not loaded from config on .NET.
rules.fix: Replace with ILogger providers.

rules.title: Printing
rules.why: Windows printing APIs and on-prem printers are not available from Linux in AWS.
rules.fix: Generate PDFs and send them to a print service / on-prem print agent.
rules.question: Which printers are used from the servers, and where are they?

rules.title: Fax
rules.why: Windows Fax Service (COM) is not available on Linux/AWS.
rules.fix: Use a cloud fax API.

rules.title: Office interop automation
rules.why: Office automation needs Office installed on Windows (and is unsupported on servers).
rules.fix: Use Open XML-based libraries.
rules.alt: Open XML SDK / ClosedXML / NPOI / EPPlus (commercial)

rules.title: Crystal Reports
rules.why: The Crystal Reports .NET runtime is Windows/.NET Framework only.
rules.fix: Re-implement reports (SSRS/PBIRS, a reporting library, or a BI tool); keep a Windows report host as an interim.
rules.alt: SSRS / Power BI Report Server; Telerik / Stimulsoft / FastReport (commercial); QuestPDF
rules.question: How many Crystal reports are in use, and can any be retired?

rules.title: SSRS web-service clients
rules.why: Calls an SSRS server that must also move (RDS SSRS option on SQL 2016-2022, PBIRS from SQL 2025, or EC2).
rules.fix: Decide where reports run; regenerate SOAP clients or use the REST API.

rules.title: PDF/HTML rendering libraries with Windows or native dependencies
rules.why: These need Windows binaries, native wkhtmltopdf builds, or have licence changes (iTextSharp 5 is AGPL/EOL).
rules.fix: Confirm the Linux story and licence; otherwise move to QuestPDF, PuppeteerSharp/Playwright (Chromium), or iText 8 (commercial/AGPL).

rules.title: SharePoint server object model / Exchange EWS
rules.why: The SharePoint server object model is on-prem/Windows only; EWS is being retired in favour of Microsoft Graph.
rules.fix: Use Microsoft Graph / CSOM REST APIs with app credentials.

rules.title: Windows time-zone IDs
rules.why: On Linux .NET resolves Windows IDs only through ICU; containers without ICU/tzdata or in invariant mode throw TimeZoneNotFoundException.
rules.fix: Store IANA IDs (or convert with TimeZoneInfo.TryConvertWindowsIdToIanaId); include tzdata and ICU in the image.

rules.title: Server-local time (DateTime.Now / Today)
rules.why: AWS hosts and containers run in UTC; logic that relied on the on-prem server's local time zone shifts (cut-offs, reports, schedules).
rules.fix: Decide the business time zone explicitly; use DateTime.UtcNow / TimeProvider and convert at the edges, or set TZ deliberately.
rules.question: Which time zone are the current servers set to, and which business rules depend on it?

rules.title: Database-server local time (GETDATE)
rules.why: RDS instances default to UTC (time zone can only be set at creation); Babelfish/PostgreSQL also run UTC by default.
rules.fix: Choose the RDS time zone at creation, or store UTC (GETUTCDATE/SYSUTCDATETIME) and convert.
rules.alt: RDS time zone setting / UTC storage

rules.title: Culture handling
rules.why: Culture data comes from ICU on Linux (formats, sorting and comparisons can differ from Windows NLS); web.config globalization settings are not applied in ASP.NET Core.
rules.fix: Set RequestLocalization explicitly; test formatting/sorting; keep ICU in images.

rules.title: Legacy TLS/SSL protocol settings
rules.why: Forcing TLS 1.0/1.1 fails against modern endpoints and compliance baselines; on .NET the OS (OpenSSL) negotiates TLS.
rules.fix: Remove protocol pinning and let the OS choose (TLS 1.2+); verify partners support TLS 1.2+.

rules.title: Certificate validation disabled
rules.why: Bypassing certificate validation hides man-in-the-middle risk and usually masks a missing internal CA.
rules.fix: Install the internal CA in the image / trust store, remove the bypass.

rules.title: Weak hashes / ciphers
rules.why: Weak algorithms fail common compliance baselines (PCI DSS, HIPAA guidance); some legacy types are obsolete on .NET.
rules.fix: Use SHA-256+ and AES-GCM; keep MD5/SHA1 only for non-security checksums.

rules.title: Insecure web.config settings
rules.why: Debug builds, detailed errors and disabled request validation weaken the production posture.
rules.fix: Disable in production configuration; review input encoding where validation is off.

rules.title: Visual Studio web application build targets
rules.why: These MSBuild targets ship with Visual Studio on Windows; the project cannot `dotnet build` on Linux as-is.
rules.fix: Convert to SDK-style (Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web) during the port.

rules.title: Pre/post-build events with Windows commands
rules.why: Windows shell commands in build steps fail on Linux build agents.
rules.fix: Replace with MSBuild tasks (Copy, Delete) or cross-platform scripts.

rules.title: Windows-only CI agents / steps
rules.why: Pipelines build on Windows agents with Visual Studio tasks.
rules.fix: Move to `dotnet` CLI steps on Linux runners (CodeBuild / GitHub Actions ubuntu).
rules.alt: AWS CodeBuild / GitHub Actions Linux runners

rules.title: Private NuGet feeds
rules.why: Private packages must be available to the new build system (and uploaded to AWS Transform when it is used).
rules.fix: Host private packages in AWS CodeArtifact; port private packages first.
rules.question: Where are the private NuGet packages built, and do we get their source?

rules.title: Coded UI / MSTest v1 tests
rules.why: Coded UI is deprecated and Windows-only; MSTest v1 needs conversion to MSTest.TestFramework.
rules.fix: Move UI tests to Playwright/Selenium; convert unit tests to MSTest v3/xUnit.

rules.title: Outdated client libraries
rules.why: Old jQuery (< 3.5) and AngularJS (EOL) carry known vulnerabilities and complicate the UI port.
rules.fix: Upgrade or replace during the UI work; serve from a bundler or CDN.

rules.title: System.Web.Optimization bundling
rules.why: Runtime bundling is not available in ASP.NET Core.
rules.fix: Bundle at build time (Vite/esbuild) or use WebOptimizer.

rules.title: ViewState reliance
rules.why: ViewState/postback state management has no equivalent outside Web Forms.
rules.fix: Redesign page state in the target UI.
